content: maria: Quick heads-up — I opened a large refactor PR (#2345) that moves a bunch of API docs from /api/ to /sdk/ and introduces redirects. Preview is up but linkcheck is failing on several anchors. Need reviewer + merge sequencing advice. sam: can you drop the preview link and list the broken anchors? also is there a separate redirects PR or is it bundled? maria: Preview: https://preview.staging.redwood.ai/preview/2345 (docs-preview-bot posted). Broken anchors I saw: `#python-client-init`, `#streaming-api-examples`, and some older anchors with spaces -> `#configuration- options` (ugh). I bundled redirects into a separate PR (#2348) so we can merge redirects first. docs-preview-bot: Preview available for PR #2345 — https://preview.staging.redwood.ai/preview/2345 — linkcheck reported 12 failures (anchors). priya: I'll take the anchor fixes (can patch in a follow-up smaller PR). Re: sequencing — we should merge redirects PR (#2348) before any large move PRs to avoid 404s for previews and external links. Also recommend splitting the big move into 2-3 focused PRs rather than one monolith. alex: Agree on splits. The preview builder times out when too many files move at once (we hit a 30m Netlify build cap last time). Suggest batch sizes ~200 files or by section (sdk clients / guides / reference). chris: To make redirects robust, let's use the redirects config we already support. Example snippet for redirects.yml we use on the platform: ```yaml - from: /api/python-client/introduction to: /sdk/python/introduction status: 301 - from: /api/streaming to: /sdk/streaming status: 301 ``` Use `status: 301` so crawlers update indexes. sam: question — some of our internal SDK snippets point to anchor `python-client-init` from product pages. If we change anchors we need backward-compatible alias anchors or else docs tests will break. Any plan for alias anchors? priya: Plan: add explicit alias anchors in the moved pages, e.g. add `` near the new `id=python-client-setup`, plus update the redirect config. I'll open PR #2350 with alias anchors and a small smoke-test script. maria: reviewers: @priya (docs), @alex (CI/build), @chris (redirects). Can we aim to merge redirects (#2348) on Thursday during 22:00 UTC maintenance window, then land move PRs Friday in batches? :hourglass_flowing_sand: alex: That window works for me. One ask: add a docs-preview smoke test that does `linkchecker` against the preview URL and fails PR if anchors missing. We currently only run a shallow check. chris: here's a quick local linkcheck command that helped me debug: `python3 -m pip install linkchecker && linkchecker --check-extern --no-follow-robots https://preview.staging.redwood.ai/preview/2345` — it highlights broken anchors. I'll add it to our docs CI job as a post-build step. sam: FYI some external partners link to old anchors; chris, are 301s enough or should we serve a tiny HTML page that points to new anchor for a while? chris: 301s are OK for the path, but path-level redirect won't fix intra-page anchor changes. For anchors we need alias anchors in the page HTML or a short-lived client-side JS that maps old anchors to new ones. Aliases are simpler and faster. priya: I'll include alias anchors in #2350. For large sections where aliasing is noisy, we can add a tiny snippet at top of page: `if (location.hash === '#old-anchor') location.hash = '#new-anchor'` — only for a few high-traffic pages. maria: sounds good. Action items: priya -> open #2350 for alias anchors + tiny smoke tests; chris -> add linkchecker step to docs CI for this set of PRs; alex -> monitor preview builder and approve build timeout increase if needed; sam -> notify partners about planned path-level redirects next week. priya: I'll tag reviewers in #2350 and add a checklist (add alias anchors, run linkchecker locally, include redirect entries in #2348). alex: quick note: when merging, please use the merge queue and hold the next batch until previews are green. If a preview fails, revert the merge of that batch and roll forward fixes. maria: Agreed. Thanks all — I'll post an updated timeline and the maintenance window calendar invite. :party-parrot: sam: Thanks — I'll also update the docs migration doc with the merge order and a short troubleshooting blurb about Netlify timeouts. chris: one last tip — when you add alias anchors, include a short comment in the source like `` so future editors don't remove them by accident. maria: great idea. closing loop soon.
